pointers.sentence: `PostgresConfig.ready` runs as the app registry is populated ([Populating the app registry](../startup/populate.md)), in this order (`django/contrib/postgres/apps.py:PostgresConfig.ready`):
It registers `RangeSerializer` with `MigrationWriter`, so that a migration can hold the driver's range values (`django/contrib/postgres/serializers.py:RangeSerializer`).

It lets `OpClass` wrap an index's expression, between `OrderBy` and `Collate` (`django/db/models/indexes.py:IndexExpression.register_wrappers`; [PostgreSQL indexes and `ExclusionConstraint`](postgres-indexes.md)).
Step 2 reaches only connection objects already made, opened or not (`django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler.all`).

The default alias's is made as soon as a model without its own `db_table` is defined, which asks it for the longest name its database allows, and all models are imported before any `ready` runs (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.contribute_to_class`).

The dictionary updated, `DatabaseIntrospection.data_types_reverse`, is the PostgreSQL backend's class attribute, so one connection found serves all (`django/db/backends/postgresql/introspection.py:DatabaseIntrospection`).
`override_settings` can install the application for a while, running `ready` again (`django/test/utils.py:override_settings.enable`).

`uninstall_if_needed` undoes steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 when a change of `INSTALLED_APPS` ends and the list then in force lacks the application (`django/contrib/postgres/apps.py:uninstall_if_needed`): at the end of an override that added it, and at neither end of one that removed it.
Ending the outer override restores the stored registry and runs no `ready` (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.unset_installed_apps`): the lookups stay unregistered though the application is installed.

`get_type_oids` asks pg_type for the numbers of a type and of its array type, returning every row found as two tuples (`django/contrib/postgres/signals.py:get_type_oids`); `get_hstore_oids` and `get_citext_oids` call it under `functools.lru_cache`, so each alias asks once, until `CreateExtension` clears the caches.
Both return at once for another vendor and for `NO_DB_ALIAS`, the connection with no database that makes test databases (`django/db/backends/base/base.py:BaseDatabaseWrapper._nodb_cursor`).

Each registers only the types pg_type returned, and of citext only the array type: under psycopg 3 on the driver's connection object; under psycopg 2 hstore globally, and citext's array type with no connection named, a comment saying a project may use the application without the extensions, and must connect before it can install one (`django/contrib/postgres/signals.py:register_type_handlers`).

`CheckPostgresInstalledMixin.check`, new in 6.0, adds the error `"postgres.E005"` to the parent's checks when `Apps.is_installed` says the application is missing (`django/contrib/postgres/utils.py:CheckPostgresInstalledMixin`).

With the application taken out, the sailings' crew field reported "'django.contrib.postgres' must be in INSTALLED_APPS in order to use ArrayField.", and their GIN index and exclusion constraint, checked for the "postgres" alias, the same error id, against the model; a model checks those only for the databases the checks are given and the router allows (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_indexes`).
Backwards, it drops the extension if it exists and clears the caches (`django/contrib/postgres/operations.py:CreateExtension`).

These subclasses of `AddIndex` and `RemoveIndex` pass `concurrently=True` to the schema editor, whose PostgreSQL version then writes `"CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY"` or `"DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS"` (`django/db/backends/postgresql/schema.py:DatabaseSchemaEditor._create_index_sql`, `django/db/backends/postgresql/schema.py:DatabaseSchemaEditor._delete_index_sql`).

The documentation says the option is not supported inside a transaction (`docs/ref/contrib/postgres/operations.txt`), and each database half first calls `NotInTransactionMixin._ensure_not_in_transaction`, which raises `NotSupportedError` in an atomic block.

What keeps the transaction away is the migration's `atomic = False`, handed by the executor to the schema editor (`django/db/migrations/executor.py:MigrationExecutor.apply_migration`); the operation's own `AddIndexConcurrently.atomic`, `False`, keeps none away (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`).

`AddConstraintNotValid`, an `AddConstraint` for a `CheckConstraint` only ([The field operations, and those on indexes and constraints](../migrations/field-operations.md)), adds `"NOT VALID"`, leaving existing rows unchecked (`django/contrib/postgres/operations.py:AddConstraintNotValid`); `ValidateConstraint` checks them, and backwards does nothing, as a comment says PostgreSQL cannot make a constraint invalid (`django/contrib/postgres/operations.py:ValidateConstraint`).

`AddConstraintNotValid`, an `AddConstraint` for a `CheckConstraint` only ([The field operations, and those on indexes and constraints](../migrations/field-operations.md)), adds `"NOT VALID"`, leaving existing rows unchecked (`django/contrib/postgres/operations.py:AddConstraintNotValid`); `ValidateConstraint` checks them, and backwards does nothing, as a comment says PostgreSQL cannot make a constraint invalid (`django/contrib/postgres/operations.py:ValidateConstraint`).
`RandomUUID` writes `"GEN_RANDOM_UUID()"` and `TransactionNow` `"CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"` (`django/contrib/postgres/functions.py`).
`ArraySubquery` is a `Subquery` inside `"ARRAY(...)"`, whose output is an `ArrayField` of the inner query's field (`django/contrib/postgres/expressions.py:ArraySubquery`).

`ArrayAgg` and `JSONBAgg` accept `distinct=True` and `order_by=...`, and give an `ArrayField` of the argument's field and a `JSONField`; `BoolAnd` and `BoolOr` a boolean (`django/contrib/postgres/aggregates/general.py:ArrayAgg`).

The statistical aggregates take two expressions, y and x, refuse with `ValueError` unless both are given, and by default give a float, but `RegrCount` an integer (`django/contrib/postgres/aggregates/statistics.py:StatAggregate`).
The general `StringAgg` reads a string as a field's name, so the old one wraps a string delimiter in `Value`, with a second warning (`django/contrib/postgres/aggregates/general.py:StringAgg`).
